title: Deciding to buy a guitar at sixteen
summary: Friends play instruments; a drummer friend steers him to guitar, and he sends away for one but finds no teachers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Well, when I was around the age, when I got around 16 years old, I had a, I used to go around with boys, most of my friends, you know, they had a few that played piano. And one boy I remember with a fine violin playing. In other words, he could play most any of the string instruments. Yes. The guitar, the violin, and the mandolin. You see? And I would be with these boys so often, till a lot of people thought I could play, although they never saw me with instruments, you know? You see? So, one day somebody asked me, say, you always with these boys, why don't you play some musical instruments? You see? So, I said, well, I never did give it a thought. So, I don't know, all of a sudden I went to a friend, Bob of mine. He played drums. His name was, we always call him Neneet, but his name was Bryant. You might have heard of that name. I don't believe so. He was from, he went to Chicago a long time ago. So, I told him, I said, Bryant. Bryant. Bryant. Bryant. Bryant. I can't think of his first name. I always said Neneet Bryant, you see? But anyway, I told him, I said, I think I'm going to buy me a mandolin. He said, I want to play a mandolin. He said, well, mandolin is a nice instrument. He said, but since you're going to learn how to play an instrument, why don't you learn something that you can make a few dollars with? I said, well, what's that? He said, get a guitar, man. He said, guitars? They use guitars in bands. They don't use no mandolin in bands. I said, well, yeah, that is a good artist. So, I did buy a guitar. I sent away for a guitar.

I was about 16, 16 or 17 years old. So, I bought the guitar. And after I got the guitar, I didn't know what to do with it. And as far as for guitar teachers, they were scarce. A lot of fellas, they played the guitar. They said, well, I'll show you what I know, but you'll see them today. Maybe they wouldn't see them no more for the next two, three weeks or a month.
